runs.text: The game tree is solved backward. If entry occurs, the incumbent receives 7 by accommodating and 3 by fighting, so accommodation is the credible response on that branch. Anticipating it, the entrant compares 6 from entering with 0 from staying out and enters. The subgame-perfect outcome is Enter, then Accommodate.

Time: 5 minutes
Outcome: Analyze repeated games, credible commitments, entry deterrence, and sequential strategic choices.
Difficulty: Advanced
THE CORE IDEA

Dynamic Strategy: Repeated Games, Credibility & Entry Deterrence examines repeated interaction, credibility, commitments, limit pricing, entry deterrence, continuation incentives, and sequential strategic reasoning. A higher continuation factor increases the weight on future consequences. Cooperation PV is 12.50; cheating path PV is 16.25. Net gain = 25 − 8 − 14 = 3 million. Aggressive competition and predation must be distinguished with evidence.
HOW TO RECOGNIZE IT
Determine whether firms interact once or expect to meet again.
Compare the immediate gain from cheating or entering with future losses from retaliation.
A threat affects behavior only when carrying it out would be credible.
Longer relationships, patience, and observable actions make cooperative outcomes easier to sustain.
WATCH OUT
Do not assume every low price is predatory. Net gain = 25 − 8 − 14 = 3 million. Aggressive competition and predation must be distinguished with evidence.
WORKED EXAMPLE: TESTING A CREDIBLE THREAT

The game tree is solved backward. If entry occurs, the incumbent receives 7 by accommodating and 3 by fighting, so accommodation is the credible response on that branch. Anticipating it, the entrant compares 6 from entering with 0 from staying out and enters. The subgame-perfect outcome is Enter, then Accommodate.
